title: Which two lines make an open figure symmetric?
description: Six open figures on a dot grid are each made of a few joined lines. Two more lines are added to each so that the finished shape has a line of symmetry.
teaching_notes: One idea: pick a mirror line, mark the matching points of the two ends, and join them. Any correct completion is fine. Watch for students who add two lines that look neat but fail the fold test.

source: Copy the following on a dot grid. For each figure draw two more lines to make a shape that has a line of symmetry.
video_script.why: The child picks a mirror line for an open figure and adds two lines by marking matching points on the other side.
video_script.substitution: Imagine a mirror line beside the open figure, mark the matching point of each end on the other side, and join them to complete the shape.
video_script.anchor: Six open figures on a dot grid, each made of a few joined lines, to be completed with two more lines
video_script.payoff_line: Pick a mirror line, then mark the matching points of the two ends.

final_answer.value: any correct completion works: pick a mirror line, draw the mirror images of the two end points, and join them to make a shape with a line of symmetry
final_answer.spoken: any correct completion works. Pick a mirror line, draw the mirror images of the two end points, and join them to make a shape with a line of symmetry

hold_back: mirror images of the two end points
never_show: a finished shape before the answer beat
maths_rules: A line of symmetry is a fold line along which one half covers the other exactly.
The mirror line can be vertical, horizontal or slanted.
Each end of the open figure has a matching point at the same distance on the other side of the mirror line.
Joining the matching points completes the two new lines.
The finished shape is closed, with four or five sides, and has the chosen mirror line as a line of symmetry.
video_script.design: One idea: choose a mirror line, then mirror the ends. Assumes the child can mirror points across a line on a grid. The six open figures stay on the board from the hook to the end.
open_questions: The six open figures are described only as a few connected line segments and could not be seen, so the method is taught generally and no particular figure is solved.
